fields.statement: Verifier claude-code-196a2d45 at 876ef85a, without editing code. Scoped tests: go test -trimpath ./internal/check/... ok; ./internal/api/... ok (544s, run from a detached worktree outside ~/code: the first run inside ~/code had no test failures but tripped the guard on writes to the enclosing root's .rhiza-root/usage.live.json, a known leak this change does not touch); TestCheckBranchNewerFormat PASS: a branch-added newer-format entry is a warning, one at the base fails, and with the option off it fails; cmd/rhiza TestScripts review-code-check, describe-golden and check* ok (describe-golden has branch_newer_format). By hand, with a scratch build in a hermetic HOME, a real run worktree and v=5 (FormatVersion+1): (a) entry committed on the run branch: rhiza check exits 1 with 'fail log ...: newer format: field v: 5, this Rhiza reads 4'; rhiza run code-check exits 0 'code-check passed' with no cause naming it, and --json shows it at severity warn; (b) the same entry committed before the merge-base: rhiza run code-check exits 1 with the cause 'rhiza check: fail log ... newer format', and check --branch-newer-format still fails it. Diff: the option only downgrades errors.Is(ErrNewerFormat) problems whose path is missing from the base listing, so other bad entries still fail; only run code-check sets it, not plain check or self-check. Gap: the testscript writes v:99 untracked rather than committing v=5, and it leaves the merge-base case to the unit test; the manual runs above cover both cases end to end.
